headline: Core growth continues; prior-year gain skews comparisons
summary_short: Revenue rose to $1,779.1M (+6.4% y/y) and operating income grew to $97.1M (+126.9% y/y), but PENN swung to a $2.3M net loss because Q1 2025 included a one-time $215.1M non-cash gain that inflated last year's net income and EBITDA.
summary_long: Retail growth came from Northeast, West, and Midwest gains — Joliet's land-based relocation and M Resort's new hotel tower — partly offset by South segment softness from new supply and weather. Interactive turned EBITDA-positive (-$10.8M vs -$89.0M) on higher hold rates, iCasino growth, and lower promotional spend as ESPN BET marketing normalized. G&A rose on HG Vora settlement costs and restructuring severance. The swing to a net loss versus prior-year net income reflects lapping Q1 2025's $215.1M non-cash financing-arrangement gain — operating income actually grew 126.9% y/y. PENN issued $600.0M of 6.75% notes due 2031 in March; cash rose to $708.0M and no shares were repurchased this quarter under the new $750.0M buyback authorization.
